title: What is crankshaft torsional vibration?

source.section: General Questions: What is crankshaft torsional vibration?

content:
Direct answer

Crankshaft torsional vibration is the twisting and rebounding of the crankshaft after combustion events.

Details

Each cylinder firing causes the connecting rod to load the crankshaft, making it twist and then unwind. If it is not controlled, the source FAQ states that this can accelerate bearing and crank-journal wear and may contribute to crankshaft failure.

Need more help?

For a specific engine combination, confirm the application in the Fluidampr finder or contact Fluidampr Technical Support.

title: Will Fluidampr correct an out-of-balance engine?

source.section: Balance: Will Fluidampr solve an out of balance condition?

content:
Direct answer

No. A vibration damper reduces crankshaft torsional vibration; it does not correct an out-of-balance rotating assembly.

Details

The supplied FAQ says that a professional balancing job is required to correct an imbalance condition.

title: What is the difference between internal and external balance?

source.section: Balance: How can you tell the difference between externally and internally balanced motors?

content:
Direct answer

An internally balanced engine uses a neutral damper. An externally balanced engine uses counterweight outside the crankshaft, including on the damper and flywheel.

Important note

Confirm the engine's balance specification before selecting a damper. Do not interchange balance configurations without source-supported application guidance.

title: How should I balance a rotating assembly used with Fluidampr?

source.section: Balance: How do I match balance the rotating assembly with a Fluidampr installed?

content:
Direct answer

Fluidampr components are precision balanced during manufacturing, so additional damper balancing is not required.

Important note

The supplied FAQ says balancing a rotating assembly with a Fluidampr installed is not recommended because a balance machine does not reproduce crankshaft torsional vibration. Follow the source-specific instructions for external-balance assemblies.

title: What press fit does Fluidampr specify for press-fit applications?

source.section: Using Fluidampr: What is the proper press fit?

content:
Direct answer

For press-fit applications, the supplied FAQ specifies a diametrical press fit of .0005 to .0015 inch.

Important warning

This guidance applies only to press-fit applications. Do not apply it to bolt-on dampers. Do not use a hammer. Use a threaded installation tool that presses the damper evenly into place.

title: Can I install Fluidampr on an early small-block Chevrolet without a damper bolt?
content:
Direct answer

No. Fluidampr does not recommend installation without a damper bolt.

Details

The supplied FAQ says the crank must be properly drilled and tapped and that the procedure requires crankshaft removal. It gives 70 ft-lbs as the bolt torque for this source-specific case.

Need more help?

Confirm the exact application with Fluidampr Technical Support before machining or installing parts.

title: What should I check before reinstalling a stored Fluidampr?
notes: Storage FAQ is source-supported but should not be treated as a universal safety inspection procedure. Escalate questionable damage.
content:
Direct answer

The supplied FAQ says a stored damper does not require routine testing when it was properly installed and not physically abused.

Check before installation

Inspect the seal surface for corrosion or pitting. The source says the surface should be smooth and free from rust and corrosion.

Important warning

If the damper was damaged in an accident, fire, or other event, do not assume it is safe. Contact Fluidampr Technical Support for a condition review.

title: Does temperature affect Fluidampr, and does it need warm-up?
content:
Direct answer

The supplied FAQ says Fluidampr does not require warm-up and provides consistent damping over its operating temperature range.

The source also states that the silicone fluid is relatively unaffected by temperature changes and will not deteriorate merely because the damper is not used for a period of time.

title: Can I paint or powder-coat Fluidampr or Streetdampr?
content:
Direct answer

Powder coating is not recommended. The supplied FAQ says the damper should never be exposed to temperatures exceeding 280°F.

Important note

Streetdampr is shipped with a corrosion inhibitor and requires a finish before installation. Follow Fluidampr technical guidance for any coating or finish decision.

title: When should I consider replacing a stock damper?
content:
Direct answer

Consider replacement when engine work changes the rotating or reciprocating mass or when the stock damper shows signs of deterioration.

Details

The supplied FAQ identifies inertia-ring movement as an obvious sign of a stock-damper problem and explains that stock dampers are tuned for stock assemblies and conditions.

title: Can Fluidampr timing marks move?

source.section: General Questions: Can timing marks move?

content:
Direct answer

No. The supplied FAQ says Fluidampr timing marks are CNC machined and cannot physically move.

Inertia-ring slippage is described as a stock-damper problem and a sign that torsional vibration may not be properly controlled.

title: Does the silicone fluid deteriorate over time?
notes: Keep service-life statements separate from the one-year limited product warranty.
content:
Direct answer

The supplied FAQ states that the silicone fluid does not deteriorate in a high-performance race or street application and is intended to last for the life of the engine.

Important note

This service-life statement is separate from Fluidampr's one-year limited warranty for defects in material and workmanship. Warranty terms and exclusions remain controlled by the formal policy.

title: When should I upgrade from Streetdampr to Fluidampr for racing?
content:
Direct answer

If you decide to competitively race a Streetdampr-equipped vehicle, review the damper requirements of the sanctioning organization.

The supplied FAQ states that Streetdampr does not receive official SFI 18.1 testing, marking, or certification required by some race-tech inspections.

title: Can Fluidampr review an application it does not currently list?
content:
Direct answer

Fluidampr can review a new application, but the supplied FAQ says damper development can be costly because engine specifications and proper fitting and testing must be evaluated.

Need more help?

Contact Fluidampr to submit an application for review. Do not treat an unlisted application as approved fitment.

title: What does Fluidampr's limited warranty cover?
content:
Direct answer

The supplied policy states that Fluidampr offers a one-year warranty to the original purchaser for defects in material and workmanship, with repair or replacement at Fluidampr's discretion.

Important notes

A sales receipt is required. The policy excludes, among other items, improper installation or maintenance, misuse, abuse, modifications, unauthorized repairs, removal or replacement cost, damage to other components, normal wear and tear, and racing or competitive use.

This limited warranty is separate from the FAQ's statement about silicone-fluid service life.

title: Where and how do I submit a Fluidampr warranty claim?
content:
Direct answer

Warranty claims must be made with the point of purchase.

If purchased from Fluidampr

Call customer service to receive a return authorization number. The policy requires the RMA number, a description of the problem, and a copy of the purchase invoice or receipt. Returns without an RMA number will not be processed.

title: What is the Fluidampr return authorization process?
content:
Direct answer

Returns must be made within 30 days of purchase, include a Fluidampr Return Authorization Number, and include a copy of the original purchase invoice.

Important notes

The policy requires original packaging for eligibility, places return freight responsibility on the customer, and states that COD returns will not be accepted.

title: How are Fluidampr international orders handled?
content:
Direct answer

The supplied policy requires international orders to be paid in full before shipment by wire transfer or money order in U.S. funds.

International customers are responsible for shipping, duties, customs, taxes, and other charges. Fluidampr uses a trackable carrier unless the customer specifies another carrier.

title: How do I find a Fluidampr by vehicle or part number?

source.filename: SEMA fitment tables and Fluidampr Finder

content:
Direct answer

Use the Fluidampr Finder for vehicle and engine application lookup, or search the Knowledge Base and product catalog by part number.

For modified, swapped, or mixed-platform combinations, verify the crank and accessory configuration with Fluidampr Technical Support before selecting a part.

title: How do I identify the LS pulley-offset group?

source.section: Choosing the Correct Harmonic Damper - LS

content:
Direct answer

The supplied LS reference groups applications by pulley offset: short, middle, and long.

Selection

Use a straightedge across the damper face and measure the offset to the center. The reference identifies short as Corvette/CTS-V/G8, middle as F-body/GTO, and long as trucks and 2010-2015 Camaro applications. Confirm the exact vehicle and engine application in structured fitment data before ordering.

Important note

The broad group labels are not unrestricted universal fitment. The reference measurement is not the WooCommerce product Depth field.

title: Which instructions apply to OEM bolts versus Fluidampr diesel bolt kits?
notes: Instruction revision conflicts for 300010. Preserve current live attachment and supplied source internally until reviewed.

source.section: Performance Diesel Installation and high-strength bolt kits

content:
Direct answer

Use the instruction sheet for the exact application and hardware. The supplied diesel guidance distinguishes OEM bolt procedures from Fluidampr high-strength bolt and friction-washer kits.

Important warning

Do not transfer torque values between applications. Follow the exact approved instruction revision and use the specified bolt, washer, lubrication, and torque procedure.

Revision review is required for part 300010 because the supplied 4NFZ02 sheet differs from the current 4NFZ01 attachment.

title: Which instructions cover Cummins drill-pin and Full Power kits?
notes: Revision conflicts: supplied 4NFG11/4NFX02 vs current 4NFG10/4NFX01. Do not replace live files automatically.

source.section: Cummins Drill Pin Kit and Full Power Kit

content:
Direct answer

The supplied materials identify the Cummins Drill Pin Kit as part 300002 and the Full Power Kit as part 300008 for the listed Cummins applications.

Important note

These source revisions require technical review against the current live attachments before any replacement. Do not infer a kit requirement for an unverified build.

title: Why do balance and crankshaft retention matter when installing a Duramax damper?

source.section: External balance, bolt kits, and drill-pin guidance

content:
Direct answer

The supplied Duramax material describes the application as externally balanced and emphasizes correct installation, clamp load, and retention.

Application notes

Use the exact application instruction and verify whether a high-strength bolt kit or drill-pin kit is supported for the build. Pinning requires precision machining and should be performed with the specified tooling and expertise.

Need more help?

For a modified or high-power combination that cannot be verified from the source, contact Fluidampr Technical Support.
